diagrams.name: architecture-overview
diagrams.prompt: Use case: infographic-diagram. Create one production-ready PNG diagram for technical documentation, landscape 1536x1024. Hand-drawn whiteboard style: clean off-white background, dark navy slightly irregular ink lines, neat highly legible hand lettering, very light blue/lavender/teal fills. Restrained, spacious, no decorations, shadows, watermarks, huge title, or long prose. Meaningful shapes: decisions are diamonds, processes are rectangles, start/end are capsules, files are document/folder icons. Queues are rows of request cards, NEVER database cylinders. Database cylinders are ONLY for a labeled SQLite database. Every arrow has an unambiguous direction, do not invent additional edges. Keep exact short labels spelled correctly. Draw a component relationship diagram, not a sequential timeline. Top row: a browser/window icon labeled "Chat · Code · Dashboard" at left, a process rectangle labeled "Node control plane" at center, a process rectangle labeled "Python crawler" at right. Connect UI to Node with a bidirectional arrow labeled "API"; Node to Python with a right arrow labeled "launch"; Python back to Node with a separate left arrow labeled "logs + records". Bottom row: folder icon "Project files" at center-left, actual cylinder "SQLite" at center-right. Node to Project files bidirectional arrow labeled "read / edit". Project files to Python arrow labeled "load code". Node to SQLite bidirectional arrow labeled "metadata + runs". Route connections around the nodes with no crossings or label collisions. No direct UI-to-Python arrow. No cloud services, no source snapshots. The diagram must clearly show the shared filesystem and metadata database as different components.

diagrams.name: agentic-runtime
diagrams.prompt: Use case: infographic-diagram. Create one production-ready PNG diagram for technical documentation, landscape 1536x1024. Hand-drawn whiteboard style: clean off-white background, dark navy slightly irregular ink lines, neat highly legible hand lettering, very light blue/lavender/teal fills. Restrained, spacious, no decorations, shadows, watermarks, huge title, or long prose. Meaningful shapes: decisions are diamonds, processes are rectangles, start/end are capsules, files are document/folder icons. Queues are rows of request cards, NEVER database cylinders. Database cylinders are ONLY for a labeled SQLite database. Every arrow has an unambiguous direction, do not invent additional edges. Keep exact short labels spelled correctly. Draw a concise sequence diagram with THREE vertical lanes labeled "Engine", "Model", "Python tools". Use horizontal message arrows and a light hand-drawn frame for the repeating exchange. Entry capsule above Engine "Goal + seeds". Within a large frame labeled "While work remains": Engine -> Model arrow "Page + state"; Model -> Python tools arrow "Choose tools"; Python tools -> Engine arrow "Observations + state". Below tools, attach three small notes without arrowheads, labeled "Queue links", "Update drafts", "Emit records". A clear arrow from "Emit records" goes to a document icon labeled "Save items", INSIDE the repeating frame, to show output during execution. Below the repeat frame on the Engine lane, one decision diamond "Queue empty + no active request?" (split short lines). Its No arrow loops back to top of repeating frame and its Yes arrow leads to an end capsule "Done". The engine alone makes the completion decision; there is NO model finish action. "Choose tools" means optional choices, do not chain the three tool categories into mandatory steps. No arrow from Done to storage. Retain a clear main sequence and plentiful whitespace.

Draw an exact decision flowchart for page routing. Top start capsule "Request URL" -> diamond "Explicit page_type?". Branch Yes to the LEFT diamond "Pass that type's patterns?". That diamond Yes -> capsule "Use explicit type", No -> capsule "Skip request". Branch No from the first diamond to RIGHT process rectangle "Find first matching type" -> diamond "Match found?". diagrams.name: item-pipeline
diagrams.prompt: Use case: infographic-diagram. Create one production-ready PNG diagram for technical documentation, landscape 1536x1024. Hand-drawn whiteboard style: clean off-white background, dark navy slightly irregular ink lines, neat highly legible hand lettering, very light blue/lavender/teal fills. Restrained, spacious, no decorations, shadows, watermarks, huge title, or long prose. Meaningful shapes: decisions are diamonds, processes are rectangles, start/end are capsules, files are document/folder icons. Queues are rows of request cards, NEVER database cylinders. Database cylinders are ONLY for a labeled SQLite database. Every arrow has an unambiguous direction, do not invent additional edges. Keep exact short labels spelled correctly. Draw the generic workflow for ONE ITEM through its configured pipeline chain. Main flow: start capsule "Extracted item" -> process rectangle "Validate model" -> predefined-process rectangle (double vertical sides) "process_item" -> diamond "Dropped?". The Dropped? Yes branch goes to terminator "Stop this item", and its edge has a small label "None / DropItem". The No branch goes to diamond "More pipelines?". More pipelines? Yes loops back to process_item with arrow label "next pipeline". More pipelines? No goes to terminator "Item processed". A small note attached without an arrowhead to process_item reads "Transform or save now". Beneath the whole diagram one short handwritten caption: "Runs for each item during the crawl". Saving happens during process_item, never after an entire crawl. Do not draw CrawlResult, database, a final Save step, or a hardcoded clean/save chain. Give decisions diamonds, terminators capsules, and validation a plain process rectangle. Crisp text and simple unambiguous arrows.

diagrams.name: async-concurrency
diagrams.prompt: Use case: infographic-diagram. Create one production-ready PNG diagram for technical documentation, landscape 1536x1024. Match a cohesive hand-drawn whiteboard series: clean off-white background, dark navy slightly irregular ink lines, neat highly legible hand lettering, very light blue/lavender/teal fills. Restrained, spacious, no decorations, watermarks, huge title, or long prose. Meaningful shapes: decisions are diamonds, processes are rectangles, start/end are capsules, files are document/folder icons. Queues are rows of request cards, NEVER database cylinders. Only an actual database may use a cylinder. Clear arrow directions, no invented connections, no crossed labels. Draw a SWIMLANE TIMELINE, left-to-right time. Top horizontal arrow labeled "Time". Three separated horizontal lanes labeled "Worker 1", "Worker 2", "Worker 3". Each lane handles ONE different response, with a sequential download followed by two sequential item-processing bars. Worker 1: "Download A" from time 0 to 2, "A1 pipelines" from 2 to 4, "A2 pipelines" from 4 to 6. Worker 2: "Download B" from 0 to 1, "B1 pipelines" from 1 to 3, "B2 pipelines" from 3 to 5. Worker 3: "Download C" from 0 to 3, "C1 pipelines" from 3 to 5, "C2 pipelines" from 5 to 7. Do NOT print numeric times; relative bar positions illustrate overlap. Download bars light blue, all pipeline bars teal. Draw small rightward arrows between consecutive bars within each lane. Bars in different lanes overlap in time, bars within one lane never overlap. Put a short handwritten note below: "Each item finishes its pipeline chain before the next". Another short note: "Responses overlap; overall item order varies". No global saving phase. Header small "Example: concurrency = 3". Wide enough columns to fit labels, no tables or database shapes.

diagrams.name: harness-execution
diagrams.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram. Create one production-ready PNG diagram for technical documentation, landscape 1536x1024. Match a cohesive hand-drawn whiteboard series: clean off-white background, dark navy slightly irregular ink lines, neat highly legible hand lettering, very light blue/lavender/teal fills. Restrained, spacious, no decorations, watermarks, huge title, or long prose. Meaningful shapes: decisions are diamonds, processes are rectangles, start/end are capsules, files are document/folder icons. Queues are rows of request cards, NEVER database cylinders. Only an actual database may use a cylinder. Clear arrow directions, no invented connections, no crossed labels. Draw a readable UML-like SEQUENCE diagram with FIVE vertical lifelines, left to right: "Chat / UI", "Project files" (folder icon), "Orchestrator", "Crawler", "items.jsonl" (document icon). Time flows downward. Exact sequence from top to bottom:
1 Chat / UI -> Project files: "Edit code"
2 Chat / UI -> Orchestrator: "Queue run"
3 Orchestrator -> Crawler: "Launch"
4 Crawler -> Project files: "Read working files"
5 A light frame labeled "During crawl" contains Crawler -> items.jsonl arrow "Append each record", and Crawler -> Orchestrator arrow "Logs"
6 Below frame Crawler -> Orchestrator arrow "Exit 0"
7 Orchestrator -> items.jsonl arrow "Import records"
8 Orchestrator -> Chat / UI arrow "Logs + records"
Show the import records arrow as reading from an already-written file AFTER successful exit, not saving items after exit. Add small footer "Records are written during the crawl; UI import follows success." No source snapshots, publishing, or cloud. Use distinct file/folder icons, rectangles for actors, thin dashed lifelines. Use only these messages; no unlabeled or doubled arrows.

Upper row titled "Metrics": small event/lightning icon with label "Crawl signals" -> process "Metrics adapter" -> process "UDP emitter" -> external receiver symbol labeled "Your receiver". Label arrow between UDP emitter and Your receiver "StatsD". Lower row titled "Logs": process "Crawler" -> process "Node collector" -> real database cylinder "SQLite" -> browser-window "Dashboard". diagrams.edit_prompt: Edit this hand-drawn technical diagram with exactly two icon corrections. Preserve all wording, positions, arrows, colors, and the two separate Metrics and Logs rows. Replace the cloud icon above 'Your receiver' with a small neutral server appliance icon (simple outlined rectangular device with two small horizontal slots), because the receiver can be local or remote. Inside the Dashboard browser window replace the bar chart with four short horizontal text lines representing log entries. No charts should appear in the Logs path. Keep everything else identical, including 1536x1024 landscape composition.

diagrams.name: state-persistence
diagrams.prompt: Use case: infographic-diagram. Create one production-ready PNG diagram for technical documentation, landscape 1536x1024. Match a cohesive hand-drawn whiteboard series: clean off-white background, dark navy slightly irregular ink lines, neat highly legible hand lettering, very light blue/lavender/teal fills. Restrained, spacious, no decorations, watermarks, huge title, or long prose. Meaningful shapes: decisions are diamonds, processes are rectangles, start/end are capsules, files are document/folder icons. Queues are rows of request cards, NEVER database cylinders. Only an actual database may use a cylinder. Clear arrow directions, no invented connections, no crossed labels. Draw a request-lifecycle TIMELINE that explains Redis persistence limitations. Four main steps left to right, with arrows connecting them: "Queued" shown as a row of small request cards with one highlighted, "Pop request" shown as one request card leaving that row, "Mark seen" shown as a fingerprint/check mark, "Download" shown as a plain process rectangle. Under Queued label "Pending in Redis". Under Pop request label "Removed from queue". Under Mark seen label "Hash stored in Redis". Under Download label "In flight". Highlight the interval AFTER Mark seen through the Download step with a pale coral bracket labeled "Interruption risk". From that bracket a red dashed downward arrow leads to a small note: "No queued request to recover" and on next line "Seen hash may prevent retry". At bottom a concise caption "Persistent state is not a full checkpoint". Do not depict successful download or automatic replay/resume. No database-shaped queue. Accurate ordering: remove queue entry FIRST, persist seen hash SECOND, start downloading THIRD. Do not put the interruption marker before pop or before marking seen.
